plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction), where bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other rational bidders do. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, overbidding risks paying more than my value warrants, and underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Truthful bidding maximizes expected profit no matter the strategies of Betty and Charles, since the mechanism is incentive-compatible. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $30.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the price you'd pay, and never pay more than your value. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Since this holds regardless of competitors' strategies, I should bid exactly my private value of $28.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, truthful bidding (bidding exactly your value) is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do, since your bid only affects whether you win, not what you pay if you win. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth to me; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $24.
